questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 89 87 84 79 72 ?
questions.solution:
Differences between successive terms are −2, −3, −5, −7 — consecutive primes. The next drop is 11, so 72 − 11 = 61.
**Answer: 61**
questions.shortcut: Spot the prime sequence in the differences.

questions.q: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V sit around a circular table facing the centre. Only one person sits between U and P when counted from the right of U. Only one person sits between P and R. Only one person sits between U and Q. Only two people sit between V and R. Only one person sits between T and Q. How many people sit between T and V when counted from the left of T?
questions.solution:
Placing the clues on a circle gives the clockwise order P, V, U, S, Q, R, T. Walking from T (left of T is the clockwise direction) the next person is P, then V — so only P sits between T and V. Answer: 1.
**Answer: 1**
questions.shortcut: Fix P, put U two places to P's anticlockwise side, then use the "one person between" clues to place R, Q and T.

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark “?” in the given series to make it logically complete? VPG 7, ZTK 11, DXO 15, HBS 19, ?
questions.solution:
In each term every letter moves +4 and the number rises by 4. HBS 19 becomes L (H+4), F (B+4), W (S+4) with 23: LFW 23.
**Answer: LFW 23**

questions.q: EGDH is related to FIFI in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JMHL is related to KOJM. To which of the following is NPRS related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
The letter shifts for EGDH → FIFI are +1, +2, +2, +1; the same pattern turns JMHL into KOJM. Apply it to NPRS: N+1 = O, P+2 = R, R+2 = T, S+1 = T → ORTT.
**Answer: ORTT**

questions.q: Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. Only five people have exams between V and T. Only two people have exams between R and T. Q has the exam immediately after R. S has the exam immediately before P but after T. How many people have exams between P and U?
questions.solution:
Five exams between V and T means they sit on Monday and Sunday; S comes after T, so T = Monday and V = Sunday. Two exams between R and T puts R on Thursday, and Q on Friday. S is just before P and after T, so S = Tuesday and P = Wednesday, leaving U on Saturday. Between P (Wednesday) and U (Saturday) are R and Q — two people.
**Answer: Two**
questions.shortcut: Place the end-pair first (Mon/Sun), then the "immediately before/after" blocks.

questions.q: Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers only. (Left) © 3 @ 8 5 1 £ 1 6 1 5 7 2 8 # € £ © € © 1 3 (Right) How many such numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
Reading the series left to right, only the first digit 3 (between © and @) has a symbol on both sides. Every other digit touches another digit or sits at an end of a run. Count = 1.
**Answer: 1**
questions.shortcut: List the symbols' positions first, then check only digits sandwiched between two of them.

questions.q: Which of the given letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the following series to make it logically complete? FZN 4 XRF 6 PJX 9 HBP 13 ?
questions.solution:
Each letter goes back 8 places (F→X, Z→R, N→F), and the numbers rise by +2, +3, +4, +5. From HBP 13: H→Z, B→T, P→H and 13 + 5 = 18, giving ZTH 18.
**Answer: ZTH 18**

questions.q: Manoj starts from Point A and drives 25 km towards South. He then takes a left turn, drives 17 km, turns left and drives 28 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 20 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
questions.solution:
Taking A as the origin: 25 km south, 17 km east, 28 km north, 20 km west, then 3 km south ends at P, which is 3 km west of A. So he must drive 3 km east.
**Answer: 3 km to the east**

questions.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A - B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A × B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A ÷ B means ‘A is the father of B’ Based on the above, how is S related to P if ‘S - K ÷ T × V + P’?
questions.solution:
S is K's wife, K is T's father, T is V's sister and V is P's mother. So S is T's mother and hence V's mother, which makes S the mother of P's mother — P's maternal grandmother (mother's mother).
**Answer: Mother’s mother**

questions.q: VASE is related to ZEOA in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, DIKW is related to HMGS. To which of the following is LQCO related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
VASE → ZEOA uses +4, +4, −4, −4, and DIKW → HMGS follows the same. Apply to LQCO: L+4 = P, Q+4 = U, C−4 = Y, O−4 = K → PUYK.
**Answer: PUYK**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.)
questions.solution:
For BXS, PLG and WSN the letter jumps are −4 then −5 (taking the alphabet cyclically for BXS). DZV breaks it: its second jump is −4, so DZV is the odd one.
**Answer: DZV**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some canals are rivers. Some rivers are oceans. Some oceans are ponds. Conclusions: (I) All ponds are rivers. (II) All oceans are canals.
questions.solution:
All the statements are 'Some' statements chained together, so nothing definite follows about 'all ponds' or 'all oceans'. Neither conclusion follows.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows**
questions.shortcut: Chains of only 'Some' premises never give an 'All' conclusion.

questions.q: Seven people F, G, H, I, V, W, and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. I sits second to the right of W. I sits third to the left of F. V sits third to the left of X. G is an immediate neighbour of both W and F. How many people sit between H and G when counted from the left of H?
questions.solution:
The conditions fix the clockwise order F, X, H, I, V, W, G. Counting from H towards its left (clockwise) to reach G passes I, V and W, so three people sit between H and G.
**Answer: Three**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations, e.g., if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 7 - 21 - 31 - 62; 9 - 27 - 37 - 74

This question is based on the ﬁve, three-digit numbers given below. (Left) 458 652 748 351 591 (Right) (Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right. What will be the resultant if third digit of the highest number is multiplied with the third digit of lowest number?
questions.solution:
The highest number is 748 (third digit 8) and the lowest is 351 (third digit 1). Product = 8 × 1 = 8.
**Answer: 8**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘CARD’ is coded as ‘4628’ and ‘NEAT’ is coded as ‘3574’. What is the code for ‘A’ in that language?
questions.solution:
The only digit common to 4628 and 3574 is 4, and the only letter common to CARD and NEAT is A. So A is coded as 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: In a certain code language, A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’, A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’, A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’ and A % B means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is E related to B if ‘E + R @ D% N # B’?
questions.solution:
E is the wife of R, R is a son of D, D is father of N, and N is B's sister. So B and R are both D's children, i.e. R is B's brother, which makes E (R's wife) B's brother's wife.
**Answer: Brother's wife**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it is numbered 2, and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. Only five people live above D. Only two people live above A. C lives below F but above A. B does not live on an even numbered floor. How many people live below C?
questions.solution:
Five above D puts D on floor 1. Two above A puts A on floor 4, so C is on 5 and F on 6. B takes an odd floor from the rest (floor 3) and E takes floor 2. Four people live below C.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (20, 46, 2) (32, 136, 24)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bananas are apples. All apples are grapes. Some grapes are oranges. Conclusions: (I) All grapes are bananas. (II) All oranges are apples.
questions.solution:
All bananas are apples and all apples are grapes, but some grapes being oranges says nothing definite about all grapes or all oranges. Neither conclusion follows.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows**

questions.q: This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below. (Left) 318 745 472 123 672 (Right) (Example: 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) (NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right.) If all the numbers are arranged in the ascending order, the position of how many numbers will remain unchanged?
questions.solution:
In ascending order the numbers are 123, 318, 472, 672, 745. Only 472 stays in the third position, so one position is unchanged.
**Answer: 1**

questions.q: If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 20 D 8 A 2 C 1 B 5 = ?
questions.solution:
Substituting the symbols: 20 − 8 ÷ 2 + 1 × 5 = 20 − 4 + 5 = 21.
**Answer: 21**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it is numbered 2 and so on till the topmost floor, which is numbered 6. Only two people live below C. Only two people live between B and C. A lives above E but below C. F does not live above D. Who lives immediately below B?
questions.solution:
Two below C puts C on floor 3. Two between B and C puts B on floor 6. A is above E and below C, so E is on 1 and A on 2. F is not above D, so F is on 4 and D on 5. Immediately below B (floor 6) is D.
**Answer: D**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (6,3,14) (14,8,27)
questions.solution:
In (6, 3, 14) and (14, 8, 27) the third number = first + second + 5. Check option (19, 12, 36): 19 + 12 + 5 = 36.
**Answer: (19,12,36)**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-clusters should replace # and % so that the pattern and relationship followed between the letter-cluster pair on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of :: ? # : IGC :: TRN : %
questions.solution:
# : IGC means each letter of # is 3 ahead of IGC, so # = LJF. The right pair applies −3 to TRN, giving QOK.
**Answer: # = LJF; % = QOK**

questions.q: Based on the alphabetical order, three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which one does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants or vowels or their position in the letter cluster)
questions.solution:
In UWR, SUP and EGB the second letter is 2 ahead of the first and the third is 5 behind the second. In KMG the third is 6 behind, so KMG is the odd one out.
**Answer: KMG**

questions.q: Each of the digits in the number 15762349 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. The position of how many digits will remain unchanged as compared to that in the original number?
questions.solution:
Ascending order of 15762349 is 12345679. Only the first digit 1 and the last digit 9 stay in place, so two positions are unchanged.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer. Q. Five students – Isha, Kavita, Meenal, Nisha, and Priti – scored different marks. Who scored the second highest? (I) Meenal scored more than Isha but less than Nisha. (II) Priti scored more than Meenal but less than Nisha.
options: Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not

Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question " Q.100 What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 32 52 68 80 88 ? A. 96 B. 94 C. 90 D. 92
questions.solution:
Combining both statements gives Isha < Meenal < Priti < Nisha, but Kavita is not placed anywhere. So the second-highest cannot be determined.
**Answer: Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question**
